% Your CV. This file decides the ORDER of things and their headings; cv.yml
% decides what goes in. app/pages/cv.vue does the same for the website.
%
% Styling: redefine the macros in preamble.tex. For deeper changes run
%   pnpm vitakit eject vitakit-cv.cls
% which copies the document class into cv-tex/, where it is yours to edit and
% takes precedence. Do not edit the copy in cv-tex/generated/ -- every build
% overwrites it.
%
% A variant (say, for one application) is just a copy of this file:
%   cp cv-tex/cv.tex cv-tex/application-xyz.tex   and change \vitadocument below.
\documentclass{vitakit-cv}
\vitadocument{cv}

% The class already loads biblatex; just point it at your .bib file.
\addbibresource{../content/publications.bib}

\input{preamble.tex}
\vitainput{profile}

\begin{document}
\vitaheader

% Prose (cover letters, statements) lives in cv-tex/prose/ as plain LaTeX and
% is included with \input, not \vitasection -- \vitasection is only for
% sections vitakit generates from content/.
% \input{prose/research-statement.tex}

\vitasection[Employment]{employment}
\vitasection[Education]{education}
\vitasection[Teaching]{teaching}

\vitapublications[Publications]{all}

\vitasection[Supervised theses]{supervision}
\vitasection[Selected talks]{talks}

\end{document}
